text:
The hardest part of adopting AI isn't the technology; it’s the people and processes around it.

As I navigate my transition into AI product management, I’m struck by how essential it is to bridge structured product management with a people-first approach. For instance, while leading a tribe of 35 at CoachHub, I found that redesigning onboarding from 15 to just 4 steps was less about streamlining the process and more about ensuring the team felt engaged and supported throughout.

In AI, this becomes even more critical. You can have the most sophisticated model, but if your team lacks the understanding or trust to leverage it, you’ll miss the mark. The data you feed into these models is only as good as the insights and expectations you set around them.

As we look to the future of AI in product management, let’s focus on fostering a culture that embraces these technologies while prioritizing human connection. After all, AI is just a tool; it’s our collective vision that will drive real impact.
